ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Flannery O'Connor

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Adult preventive visit; no new complaints. [S]

Ms. O'Connor returns for her yearly preventive visit, five months into treatment for lupus nephritis. Her joints and skin are quiet, and the three-month results showed the urine protein falling by half. She is on prednisone 7.5 mg a day, tapering. The bladder infection in June cleared with nitrofurantoin. She writes five mornings a week and has finished a draft of her novel. She completed the health risk assessment before the visit. [S]

tr.td: Systemic lupus erythematosus with class III lupus nephritis on treatment
Mycophenolate 1000 mg twice daily; belimumab 200 mg weekly; hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily; losartan 25 mg daily; prednisone 7.5 mg daily, tapering; vitamin D3 1000 units daily

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-05; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: No ulcers; teeth in good repair
Regular rhythm; no murmur or rub; no edema
No synovitis; full, painless hip movement
No malar or discoid rash; no suspicious moles

Pain and swelling of the small joints of both hands, the wrists, and the knees for three months, with an hour of morning stiffness, evening fevers to 38 °C, fatigue, and a red rash over the cheeks and nose after sun; told elsewhere it might be rheumatoid arthritis; cause to be established

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus at the second visit; joint pain in 1950 with suspected rheumatoid arthritis is documented (D).
Protein and blood in the urine: protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.6 g/g and 18 red cells per high-power field, with normal creatinine; cause to be established
S — Synthetic presenting finding at the index visit, superseded by the kidney biopsy diagnosis at the third visit.

Systemic lupus erythematosus, classified by the EULAR/ACR criteria (ANA 1:640 homogeneous; score 32 before the biopsy): inflammatory arthritis, acute cutaneous lupus (malar rash), fever, leukopenia with lymphopenia, mild thrombocytopenia, low C3 and C4, anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm positive; antiphospholipid antibodies and lupus anticoagulant negative
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis and results; her systemic lupus erythematosus, diagnosed in Atlanta in late 1950 or early 1951, is documented (D), but no finding from her lifetime is used.

Lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS class III (A), focal proliferative, on kidney biopsy: endocapillary proliferation in 9 of 30 glomeruli, activity index 6 of 24, chronicity index 1 of 12, full-house immunofluorescence; no thrombotic microangiopathy; urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.8 g/g; normal kidney function
S — Synthetic biopsy result and class; kidney involvement is documented at the end of her life, but no kidney finding from her lifetime is used.
Long-term glucocorticoid treatment for lupus nephritis, tapering to 5 mg a day or less
S — Synthetic treatment status; the documented steroid harm in her life is the reason the episode keeps glucocorticoids low.
Long-term mycophenolate mofetil, with belimumab, for lupus nephritis; bone and infection protection in place
Levonorgestrel intrauterine system for highly effective contraception during mycophenolate treatment
S — Synthetic contraception, chosen by the patient.

Acute cystitis on mycophenolate, belimumab, and prednisone 15 mg: two days of burning, frequency, and urgency without fever or flank pain; urine culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; resolved with seven days of nitrofurantoin
S — Synthetic common infection in an immunosuppressed young woman; coded without hematuria because the persistent hematuria is from her nephritis.

Adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and a written prevention plan given. Depression screen negative; AUDIT-C 1. [S]
Next preventive visit in one year.

Systemic lupus erythematosus on immunosuppression (M32.19). Clinically quiet. Infection prevention is complete for the year with today's influenza vaccine; COVID-19 vaccine due. [S]
Continue the rheumatology plan; six-month assessment this month.

Cervical cancer screening while immunosuppressed. Cytology two years ago was normal. Women on immunosuppression have a higher risk of cervical precancer, so yearly screening is advised while she is on mycophenolate. [S]
Cervical cytology with HPV testing today; result by portal message.

Guideline basis: Medicare Preventive Services reference: visit templates, screening cascades, and documentation elements (2026); USPSTF A and B Recommendations (2026); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026)

Follow-up: Cervical screening result by portal message. Six-month lupus nephritis assessment this month. COVID-19 vaccine next week. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-26: six-month response assessment: complete renal response; prednisone 5 mg; pregnancy planning. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 15 minutes, with her consent. She has named a close friend as her health care agent and completed a written health care directive today, now scanned into the chart. Her first instruction is that she is to be told the truth about her illness directly, and that no clinician is to give her information to anyone else before giving it to her. She would want full treatment for a lupus flare or an infection; she would not want prolonged life support if she could not expect to recover the ability to read and write. [S]
